## What this notebook did not do

Where a step needed a package or model this environment does not ship, the cell said so and continued. An existing message means that step did not run — do not read its absence as a clean result.

Next steps that belong elsewhere:

- **Raw reads to counts** — Cell Ranger and the alignment tools are wrappers, not notebook cells.
- **Differential expression between conditions** — write the pseudobulk tables at the end, then run the `deseq2` wrapper on them.
- **scVI integration, CellTypist reference models, Scanorama, enrichment (gseapy), spatial** — packages or runtime model downloads this environment omits; use a project environment for them.
- **R/Seurat route** — the sibling seurat-workflow skill renders the same analysis on Seurat objects.
attribution: Step order and explanations follow the NBIS workshop-scRNAseq scanpy labs (CC-BY-4.0 per the repository LICENSE, NBIS Sweden) — https://nbisweden.github.io/workshop-scRNAseq/. The code is original to this plugin and runs in the private plugin:scanpy environment (scanpy 1.13): no install cells, no Colab paths, and the config cell is the single place to tune parameters.

min_genes.comment: minimum genes per cell; lower it for shallow libraries

max_genes.comment: maximum genes per cell; above this a cell is a likely doublet

min_counts.comment: minimum UMIs per cell; below this a droplet is likely empty

max_counts.comment: maximum UMIs per cell; above this a cell is a likely doublet

mt_max.comment: maximum mitochondrial percent; stressed cells exceed it

ribo_pattern.comment: ribosomal gene regex; fraction is context, not a gate

hb_pattern.comment: hemoglobin gene regex; marks blood contamination

quantiles.comment: distribution quantiles reported for each QC metric

detect_doublets.comment: run Scrublet; the filter cell removes flagged cells

doublet_expected_rate.comment: expected doublet rate; null derives it from loaded cell count

normalization.comment: scanpy route normalizes by library size then log1p

n_hvg.comment: number of variable genes to keep

hvg_flavor.comment: HVG flavor on the counts layer; seurat_v3 needs scikit-misc, which this environment ships

regress_vars.comment: obs covariates to regress out before scaling; empty by default

dims.comment: PCs used for neighbours and UMAP

resolution.comment: clustering granularity; a list sweeps several resolutions

seed.comment: random seed, so clustering and embedding repeat exactly

batch_key.comment: obs column naming the batch; integration skips when absent

batch_method.comment: integration method: harmony, combat or bbknn (bbknn needs a project environment)

group_by.comment: obs column defining the groups for markers and annotation

test_use.comment: marker test: wilcoxon, t-test, t-test_overestim_var or logreg

logfc_threshold.comment: minimum absolute log2 fold change for a marker

min_pct.comment: minimum fraction of group cells expressing a marker

top_n.comment: markers printed and plotted per group

panel_path.comment: marker panel JSON; null uses the built-in example panel

mapping_path.comment: cluster -> label JSON overriding the panel scores

label_column.comment: obs column written with the cell-type labels

min_score.comment: minimum panel score; below it a cluster stays unassigned

annotation_method.comment: panel scoring or celltypist (needs a project environment)

group_column.comment: condition column for pseudobulk units; null = one column per sample

min_cells.comment: minimum cells for a pseudobulk unit to be kept

min_samples_per_group.comment: warn when a condition has fewer samples than this

min_count.comment: count at which a gene counts as expressed in a pseudobulk column

min_cells_expressing.comment: pseudobulk columns expressing a gene needed to keep it

counts_output.comment: pseudobulk counts table for the deseq2 wrapper

samples_output.comment: pseudobulk sample sheet for the deseq2 wrapper

root_cluster.comment: trajectory root; null takes the first cluster — choose from biology

interactions_path.comment: optional ligand-receptor TSV/CSV (ligand, receptor); null uses curated starter pairs

ccc_min_pct.comment: minimum fraction of cells expressing every subunit in sender/receiver group

ccc_perms.comment: cell-label permutations for ligand-receptor empirical p-values

ccc_fdr.comment: BH FDR cutoff for significant ligand-receptor interactions

ccc_output.comment: output TSV path for tested ligand-receptor interactions

regulons_path.comment: optional TF regulon table (source/tf, target/gene, weight) or .gmt; null uses curated 18-TF starter panel

regulon_method.comment: TF regulon scoring method: aucell or ulm

regulon_top_frac.comment: top expressed gene fraction for AUCell recovery curve

regulon_min_targets.comment: minimum matched target genes to score a TF regulon

regulon_output.comment: output TSV path for cell-by-TF regulon activity scores

figures_dir.comment: directory for the PNG copies of every plot

plot_tag.comment: suffix for the QC plots; the filter pass re-tags them after

steps.title: Score clusters against a marker panel

1.title: Lab 01 — Quality control
1.intro:
Quality control on raw counts: per-cell gene/UMI/mitochondrial distributions,
Scrublet doublet detection, and threshold filtering with a report of what each
threshold removed.

Starts from a 10x matrix directory, a Cell Ranger .h5, or an .h5ad. Adapted from the
NBIS workshop-scRNAseq scanpy labs (CC-BY-4.0); the code is original to this plugin.

2.title: Lab 02 — Dimensionality reduction
2.intro:
The QC chain plus normalization, highly variable genes (seurat_v3 on counts),
scaled PCA on the variable genes, Leiden clustering and UMAP — the scanpy
counterpart of the Seurat preprocess step.

Adapted from the NBIS workshop-scRNAseq scanpy labs (CC-BY-4.0).

3.title: Lab 03 — Data integration
3.intro:
Multi-sample data: after PCA, Harmony (or ComBat) removes the batch axis, and
before/after UMAPs colored by batch show whether integration mixed the samples
without erasing biology. Without a batch column the integration cell says so and
the chain continues uncorrected.

Adapted from the NBIS workshop-scRNAseq scanpy labs (CC-BY-4.0).

4.title: Lab 04 — Clustering and cluster markers
4.intro:
The integrated chain plus Leiden clustering at the configured resolution and
per-cluster marker tables (Wilcoxon), the evidence a cell-type call must rest on.

Adapted from the NBIS workshop-scRNAseq scanpy labs (CC-BY-4.0).

5.title: Lab 05 — Differential expression, sample-level
5.intro:
Cluster markers are exploratory: cells from one donor are not independent
observations. This chain adds pseudobulk aggregation per sample so a condition
contrast can be tested with the deseq2 wrapper on the written tables.

Adapted from the NBIS workshop-scRNAseq scanpy labs (CC-BY-4.0).

6.title: Lab 06 — Cell type annotation
6.intro:
Score every cluster against a marker panel (panel mean minus the rest, so
panel sizes stay comparable), inspect the margins and the dot plot, then write
the labels back. A cluster with no evidence stays unassigned.

Adapted from the NBIS workshop-scRNAseq scanpy labs (CC-BY-4.0).

7.title: Lab 07 — Trajectory inference
7.intro:
The annotated chain plus PAGA and diffusion pseudotime: a coarse graph of
cluster relationships and a pseudotime ordering rooted in the first cluster.
Edit the root in the cell if biology says another cluster starts the process.

Adapted from the NBIS workshop-scRNAseq scanpy labs (CC-BY-4.0).

8.title: Lab 08 — Cell-cell communication
8.intro:
The annotated chain plus heteromeric ligand-receptor cell-cell communication
screening (CellPhoneDB subunit-minimum rule + cell-label permutation FDR) on the
unscaled lognorm snapshot, producing a sender-receiver hub heatmap and top L-R
dotplot. Pass interactions_path for an exhaustive OmniPath/CellPhoneDB catalog.

9.title: Lab 09 — TF regulon activity (AUCell / ULM)
9.intro:
The annotated chain plus transcription factor regulon activity scoring
(AUCell recovery AUC or weighted ULM t-statistic) on the unscaled lognorm layer,
storing X_regulon in obsm and computing per-group differential activity (BH FDR)
and a top-TF heatmap.
